doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Drummer influences: Sonny Payne, Shelly Manne, Woodyard and others
summary: He names big band drummers he loved as a teenager and later Blakey, Max, Philly Joe and Roy Haynes.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well who were the people that influenced you, drummers, along the way? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

Well in the big bands, when I was in high school, that was when I first started playing, I was really drawn to big bands and the Kenton band and of course Basie and Duke, all those guys. Sonny Payne, I remember seeing him when I was just starting out and I was just floored. I thought he was —
He had a lot of style, didn’t he?

Oh he was just — I mean he had it all, you know, for a big band. I mean he was just so dynamic. Here this band is just quietly steaming along and all of a sudden it explodes right in front of your eyes. It would just like — when you’re a kid especially it would just throw you back. And then he was just so much fun to watch. And I don’t play anything like that. But he knocked me out. And of course then later on Shelly Manne and Mel Lewis and Woodyard, who I loved, Sam Woodyard. You know, that kind of thing. And then I started listening to all kinds of — I got more into Blakey and Max and Philly Joe and Roy Haynes and those guys. And there are just so many guys. And then all the new guys that come along, it just gets better and better technically.
